newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: CAM selling disk drive unit stake.
newsitem.headline: CAM selling disk drive unit stake.

text.p: Singapore's CAM International Holdings Ltd said on Monday that it is selling a 52.5 percent stake in its hard disk drive subsidiary to IPC Corp Ltd and a Malaysian businessman for 17 million ringgit.

CAM officials told a news conference that the company will sell 37.5 percent in CAM Precision Component (Penang) Sdn Bhd to businessman Hamzah Mohd Noor, who is a director at the unit, and another 10 percent stake to IPC.
A further five percent will be sold to Essex Investment (Singapore) Pte Ltd, the parent company of IPC.
Following the divestment, CAM will be left with a 47.5 percent stake in the contract manufacturing subsidiary, located in northern Penang state.

The stake sale to Hamzah was to comply with Malaysia's investment policy on bumiputera (ethnic Malay) participation, while IPC, a large personal computer manufacturer, will be "a captive customer," said Lee Kwong Loong, chief executive officer of CAM Precision.
CAM said the sale of the unit to IPC is conditional on IPC agreeing to buy 35,000 units of the hard disk drives a month from the Penang company.
